title: ExecutionResult
description: The structured answer an agent adapter owes the runner (release 3.8, H38-03). Handed to `codex exec --output-schema` so the provider emits this shape directly instead of prose the runner has to guess at. Mirrors New-ExecutionResult in backend/modules/execution/Execution.WorkPacket.ps1; the PowerShell constructor is the authority and this file must be changed with it.

taskId.description: The queue entry / run identifier this result answers for.

executionId.description: One attempt at that task. Distinct from taskId once a task is resumed.

provider.description: Which provider produced this. Never inferred by the reader.

providerSessionId.description: The provider's own thread/session identifier, so a run can be resumed on the same session. Null when the provider did not report one -- an absent identifier is not an error.

status.description: capacity_exhausted is a first-class outcome, not a kind of failure: a provider limit means the work was never attempted, so recording it as failed would blame the task for the subscription's state.

passed.description: Tri-state on purpose: true, false, or null for "no verification ran". Collapsing null into false would report an unverified run as a failed one, which is a different and much louder claim.

commands.description: The commands actually run, verbatim, so a reviewer can re-run them.

native.description: Whatever the provider reported, in the provider's own units, kept unconverted. Deliberately unconstrained: the spec forbids inventing a token conversion for a subscription allowance, so this stays opaque.

tokensObserved.description: A count only when the provider genuinely gave one. Null means "not measured", which is a different claim from 0.

risks.description: Named conditions a reviewer should know about, e.g. provider-limit.

summary.description: What happened, in the agent's own words. Bounded, because it lands in a run summary an operator reads rather than in a log.

source.description: adapter = parsed from provider output; interactive = recorded by the runner because a human watched the session.
